name: Swamp of Sorrows
summary: Green dragonspawn guard the drowned Temple of Atal'Hakkar beneath the Pool of Tears. Between Deadwind Pass and the Blasted Lands, this salt-crusted mire holds dangerous wildlife and the Horde garrison at Stonard. The Alliance has no safe haven here.

sections.title: A Drowned History
sections.body:
The Swamp of Sorrows was once the northern half of the vast Black Morass. After the Gurubashi Empire shattered, fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire and built the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. They meant to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer, their bloodthirsty loa. The Aspect Ysera sensed the danger and drowned the cursed pyramid beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were set to watch over it.

Later, the Dark Portal's cataclysm scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands. The northern fen took its sorrowful name.

sections.title: Outposts and Broken Exiles
sections.body:
Stonard is the swamp's main foothold for settled folk. First established during the First War alongside Rockard and Kyross, both now ruined, it was rebuilt under Thrall as the Horde's southernmost staging ground in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Strange wanderers cross the fen beyond its palisades. Draenei stranded on Azeroth grew homesick and mad, becoming feral Lost Ones. At the Harborage, a small enclave of lucid Broken exiles remains wary, yet willing to trade peacefully with travelers.

sections.title: The Sinking Mire
sections.body:
Predators make every crossing of the Swamp of Sorrows dangerous. Deep bogs conceal lunging crocolisks, venomous spiders, prowling swamp jaguars, and bog beasts coated in marsh debris. Vicious murlocs crawl through coastal caverns and along the Misty Reed Strand.

Salt-laden tides creep inland and crust rotten logs with brine. Farther east, aggressive elite dragonspawn guard the approaches to the Sunken Temple in Sorrowmurk. They attack anyone who strays near their vigil.

faq.q: How do I reach the Swamp of Sorrows?
aliases: how to get to swamp of sorrows
faq.answer: The common overland route runs east from Darkshire in Duskwood, through haunted Deadwind Pass, and down into the marsh. From the south, follow the main road north out of the Blasted Lands.

faq.q: Why is the Temple of Atal'Hakkar underwater?
faq.answer: Centuries ago, the Atal'ai priesthood tried to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer into Azeroth. Ysera, Aspect of the Green Flight, discovered their demonic blood rites and drowned the temple in the bog to avert disaster. Green dragonspawn guard its submerged halls.

Stonard began as one of the Orcish Horde's first settlements after it crossed the Dark Portal during the First War. Fighting ravaged the outpost, but Thrall recently ordered it reclaimed and rebuilt to anchor Horde logistics near the Blasted Lands.

faq.q: Are there any Alliance settlements here?
faq.answer: The Swamp of Sorrows has no Alliance settlements, guards, or flight paths. If you travel through the mire, base yourself in Darkshire to the west or Nethergarde Keep to the south.

faq.q: Who are the strange mutated humanoids in the swamp?
faq.answer: These strange humanoids are draenei stranded on Azeroth after the Dark Portal collapsed. Cut off from their world, most fell to despair and madness and became hostile Lost Ones. A small group of sane Broken exiles found refuge at the Harborage in the northwest, choosing neutral survival over mindless rage.
Sorrowmurk is the dense marshland east of the Pool of Tears. Elite green dragonspawn and whelps patrol there, violently turning mortals away to protect the secrets of the Sunken Temple.

angles.text: Stonard is your vital forward redoubt in the southern continent. Wyvern routes connect it directly to Kargath, Flame Crest, Grom'gol Base Camp, Booty Bay, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades.
With no outpost to rally behind, you face an isolated, hostile journey through the swamp. Prepare carefully in Darkshire or Nethergarde Keep before setting out.
The marsh is one of Azeroth's few rich sources of blindweed. You can also find plenty of liferoot, fadeleaf, and stranglekelp.
Along the mountainous crags on the swamp's northern and southern edges, you can gather iron, gold, mithril, and truesilver.
The sunken ruins of Atal'Hakkar recall the dark blood magic that fractured the Gurubashi Empire and drew the Dragon Aspects' wrath.
